hedge_knight: This week's lessons were on archery. Apparently, {scion} is a deft shot.
The trainees spent the week sparring. You've caught some boys in town staring at {scion} while rubbing their bruises.
Ser Bedivere has had {scion} doing calisthenics all week. Last night, she made you carry her to bed like a child.
This week was jousting practice. {scion} limped back home, rubbing her shoulder. "It looks so easy at the tournaments"
Ser Bedivere spent the week drilling {scion} in footwork. By his own account, he once out-stepped thirty men at Oakhaven.
{scion} reports that Ser Bedivere's stand at Oakhaven now features forty men and a bear.
Ser Bedivere taught {scion} how to fall without breaking anything. She demonstrated on the stairs at supper.
Sebastian bested {scion} at the pell twice this week. She bested him on the third day, and has mentioned it several times since.
"A knight is a shield before she is a sword," Ser Bedivere told {scion}. Then he had her carry one around the yard until dusk.
{scion} spent a day polishing Ser Bedivere's breastplate. Every dent has a story, and he told her all of them.
Ser Bedivere showed {scion} how to hold a line beside others. She talked about flanks and shield-walls all through supper.
Ser Bedivere's knee gave out mid-lesson. {scion} pretended not to notice, and he pretended he was resting it on purpose.
hermit: Diogenes put {scion} to work transcribing some of the ancient texts. Her fingertips are stained with ink.
{scion} asked Diogenes whether dogs go to Heaven. He answered, "Moo!"
Diogenes instructed {scion} in Latin. When you asked her what she learned, all she said was, "semper ubi sub ubi"
"Do, or do not," Diogenes sagely instructed, "there is no 'try'."
Diogenes held this week's lessons from the mouth of his barrel. {scion} says the view is better than you would think.
Diogenes sent {scion} through the market at noon with a lit lantern, looking for an honest man. She did not find one either.
{scion} asked Diogenes what a ruler needs most. He told her to stand out of his sunlight. She is still deciding if that was the answer.
Diogenes and Serena argued doctrine all week. {scion} says she learned more from the arguing than from the lessons.
Diogenes had {scion} sit in silence for an entire afternoon. She came home unusually thoughtful, and unusually hungry.
Diogenes made {scion} copy the same psalm three times, then asked her what it meant. She is still working on it.
Diogenes grumbled that {scion} asks too many questions. Then he lent her a book he swears he never owned.
{scion} brought Diogenes a loaf of bread. He gave half to a stray dog and called it the best lesson of the week.
smuggler: Hancock worked with {scion} on the arts of legerdemain. He said that she took to it naturally, perhaps a little much.
Hancock had {scion} practicing her prestidigitation down by the docks. Apparently the town guard were not amused.
"Always watch the hands and the eyes," Hancock advised. "that's the fastest way to read a man's intent."
{scion} and Hancock practiced running cons in the marketplace. The two swore they returned all the money taken.
Hancock taught {scion} to pick a lock with a hairpin. You have started counting your hairpins.
Hancock had {scion} slip through the crowded market without brushing a single elbow. Nicole tagged along and made it a race.
{scion} learned to spot loaded dice this week. Hancock says every ruler needs that skill, especially around tax collectors.
Hancock taught {scion} the thieves' cant. She has been leaving chalk marks on the gatepost.
Hancock claims he once outran a magistrate's whole cavalry on a stolen mule. {scion} believes about half of it.
{scion} watched Hancock haggle a fishmonger down to nothing, then quietly pay the man double on the way out.
Hancock taught {scion} to read a room: who is armed, who is drunk, and who is pretending to be both.
{scion} came home with a purse you don't recognize. She swears Hancock gave it to her as a "teaching aid."

success: {scion} mucked out every stall and earned a nuzzle from the grey mare.
Hard work, honest pay. {scion} came home smelling of hay and horse.
Olaf told {scion} a joke about a bishop and a goat. She will not repeat it, but she hasn't stopped smiling.
{scion} broke nothing and lost nothing, which Olaf says puts her ahead of the last three stablehands.
The grey mare let {scion} brush her mane this week. Olaf claims he trained the horse to do that. He did not.
{scion} spent the week hauling water and pitching hay. She ate two helpings at supper and fell asleep at the table.
Olaf somehow lost a wager to a draft horse. {scion} would not explain, but she laughed all through supper.
{scion} rode one of the post horses around the paddock while Olaf wasn't looking. Or while he pretended not to.
A merchant's courser threw a shoe in the yard, and {scion} calmed it before Olaf had finished swearing.
"Horses are like lords," Olaf told {scion}. "Feed them, brush them, and follow behind with a shovel."
{scion} carried a dozen tankards at once and spilled not a drop.
The regulars sang her praises, and their tips were generous.
Helga taught {scion} to carry four tankards on one arm. She managed three, and Helga called it a fine start.
{scion} learned every regular's usual this week. Helga says that's the whole job, really.
Two mercenaries started a brawl. {scion} saved the good chairs first, just as Helga taught her.
{scion} came home with a pocketful of coppers and a song about a one-eyed miller stuck in her head.
Helga let {scion} help in the kitchen. The mutton stew was, by every account, edible.
{scion} talked a drunk tinker out of a fight and into a bowl of stew. Helga gave her the last honey cake.
Nicole stopped by the alehouse, and the two of them worked the floor like they were children running the market again.
A traveling minstrel played all night, and {scion} kept the ale flowing without spilling a drop.
failure: {scion} broke three cups and a stool. Helga docked her wages.
A brawl broke out, and {scion} hid behind the barrels until it was over.
{scion} brought table four the mutton. Table four had ordered fish. Then table four started a fight.
A mercenary pinched {scion}, and she emptied a tankard over his head. Helga approved. The owner docked her wages.
{scion} watered down the regulars' ale by mistake. The regulars noticed. Regulars always notice.
{scion} slipped on a spilled pint and took a tray of bowls down with her. Helga laughed, then handed her the broom.
{scion} got so caught up in a sailor's story that the whole east side of the room went dry.
{scion} forgot to tap the new cask, and the alehouse ran out of ale on market day.
{scion} lost count of a drovers' tab, and they slipped out before anyone noticed.
A brawl broke out, and {scion} saved the cheap chairs. Helga has not let her forget it.

success: {scion} walked the walls till dawn and caught a pig thief red-handed.
Captain Baldwin let {scion} carry the lantern at the head of the patrol.
Captain Baldwin found {scion}'s halberd polished and her boots laced at dawn inspection. He nodded once, which is apparently high praise.
{scion} turned back a pair of drunken drovers at the gate without raising her voice.
{scion} spent the week on the walls. She now knows every loose stone and every guard's snore by heart.
Baldwin drilled the watch until they could bar the gate in under a minute. {scion} was first to her post every time.
{scion} found a lost child out past curfew and walked her home instead of writing her up. Baldwin pretended not to hear about it.
A cart overturned on the bridge, and {scion} had the road clear before the captain arrived.
{scion} came home smelling of torch smoke and cold iron, and recited all thirty watch rules at supper.
Sebastian and {scion} walked the night patrol together. Nothing happened, and they argued about it all the way.
failure: {scion} fell asleep at her post. Captain Baldwin was not amused.
A fox got into the hen coops on her watch. The farmers blamed the girl.
{scion} let a peddler through the gate without checking his cart. Baldwin checked it later, and found a goat.
{scion} forgot the password and challenged Baldwin himself at the gate. He made her recite it a hundred times.
{scion} dropped her halberd off the wall. It landed point-down in the reeve's turnip patch.
Baldwin caught {scion} chatting with the gatekeeper instead of watching the road. Extra drill for a week.
{scion}'s lantern went out on night patrol, and she spent an hour lost in a lane she has known since she was six.
A drunk talked his way past {scion} with a story about his sick mother. His mother lives in the alehouse.
{scion} rang the alarm bell at a shadow. The shadow was a cow. The whole village is awake, and the cow is fine.
Baldwin lectured {scion} for an hour on how the law is a wall. She says she understood it after the first ten minutes.

success: {scion}'s lettering drew a nod from Deacon Jerome himself.
She finished a page of the psalter without a single blot.
Deacon Jerome found no errors in {scion}'s copy of the psalter. He checked it twice to be sure.
{scion} illuminated her first capital letter, a little gold-leafed dragon. Deacon Jerome called it "adequate," which the brothers say is unheard of.
{scion} copied a whole chapter of the lives of the saints. She can now recite most of them, whether you ask or not.
Serena quizzed {scion} on doctrine all week. {scion} got most of the answers right, and argued about the rest.
{scion} mixed a batch of oak-gall ink that Deacon Jerome declared fit for a bishop's letters.
{scion} found a misplaced psalm in an old codex. Deacon Jerome took the credit, but he did say thank you.
The scriptorium was quiet as snow all week. {scion} came home with steady hands and a calm mind.
{scion} mended a cracked binding with glue and patience. The brothers say she could take the cowl if she wanted.
failure: {scion} knocked over an inkwell onto a fresh page. Deacon Jerome sighed deeply.
She dozed during vespers and was sent home early.
Deacon Jerome caught {scion} copying one of Diogenes' quips into the margin. She spent the rest of the week scraping vellum.
{scion} misspelled "Jerusalem" three times on one page. Deacon Jerome had her write it out fifty times.
{scion} drew a little horse in the margin of the gospels. Deacon Jerome did not find it charming.
{scion} asked Deacon Jerome why the Church says one thing and Diogenes another. She was sent to scrub the floor.
A candle tipped onto {scion}'s page and burned straight through a saint. Deacon Jerome prayed for the saint, then for her.
{scion} spent the week copying the wrong book. Deacon Jerome didn't notice for two days, and was furious with both of them.
{scion} sneezed on a fresh sheet of gold leaf. It is now somewhere in the rafters.
Serena reported {scion} for laughing during vespers. {scion} insists Serena started it.

rest_home: {scion} slept late, then spent the afternoon mending by the hearth.
A quiet week. {scion} read aloud to {player} by candlelight.
{scion} helped you mend the fence, then told you exactly how Ser Bedivere would have done it.
A rainy week at home. You and {scion} played draughts by the fire. She cheated, and so did you.
{scion} slept until noon three days running. You let her.
{scion} cooked supper. It was mostly edible, and she was very proud of it.
Nicole came by, and the two of them spent the afternoon on the roof, talking about nothing and everything.
{scion} asked you about her mother. You told her what you could.
{scion} spent the week in the garden, and came in each evening with dirt under her nails and color in her cheeks.
You told {scion} a story from your soldiering days. She has heard it before, but she listened anyway.
bathhouse: {scion} came home pink-cheeked and smelling of rosemary.
The bath-wife scrubbed {scion} raw and charged double for the soap.
{scion} soaked until the water went cold, and came home loose-limbed and yawning.
According to the bathhouse gossip, the reeve's cook is in love with the miller's wife. {scion} reported all of it in detail.
{scion} had her hair washed in chamomile. She smells like a meadow, and she knows it.
The steam left {scion} so drowsy she nodded off on the walk home. You carried her the last stretch.
Helga was at the bathhouse too. {scion} says it is strange to see her without four tankards in hand.
An old bath-wife with hands like iron worked the knots out of {scion}'s shoulders. She swears she grew an inch.
The bathhouse was nearly empty, and {scion} had the hot pool to herself all afternoon.
Someone stole {scion}'s shoes at the bathhouse. Thanks to Hancock's lessons, she got them back before she left.
shrine: {scion} lit a candle and sat in the cool dark until her thoughts stilled.
The old priest blessed her, then asked after {player}'s health.
{scion} lit a candle for the old king. She did not say why, and you did not ask.
{scion} kept vigil at the shrine through the night, and came home lighter.
The shrine-keeper taught {scion} a hymn for the Conjunction. She hums it while she works.
{scion} left a coin at the shrine for everyone she knows. It cost more than she expected.
Diogenes was at the shrine too, arguing with a statue. {scion} says he seemed to be winning.
{scion} prayed for patience with Serena. Then, after a moment, for Serena's patience with her.
{scion} walked the pilgrims' path to the hilltop shrine and watched the sun set over the valley.
A week of quiet prayer. {scion} doesn't know if anyone was listening, but she feels better for having spoken.
banquet: Roast swan, honeyed figs and minstrels. {scion} danced until the candles guttered.
{scion} ate too much marchpane and regretted none of it.
{scion} danced with a minor baron's son, who stepped on her toes nine times. She counted.
Ser Bedivere told the tale of Oakhaven to the whole banquet hall. By the end, it was sixty men.
{scion} tried every dish on the table, including one that may have been a peacock.
The minstrels played until dawn, and {scion} now knows all the bawdy verses. You have decided not to ask where from.
A visiting abbess sat beside {scion} and asked her opinion on everything. {scion} is still flattered.
Sebastian and Serena came to the banquet too, and {scion} survived a whole evening of capital manners.
{scion} won a game of riddles with a joke she learned from Olaf. The bishop at the high table pretended not to understand it.
A juggler set his own sleeve on fire, and {scion} laughed so hard she had to be helped from the table.

idle: I wonder what lies beyond the hills...
Ser Bedivere's stories get longer every time he tells them.
Nicole hasn't come by in a while...
Do the stars really care when the Conjunction comes?
I had that dream again. The one with the fire.
Sebastian thinks he's so clever. Serena actually is.
I'd like to see the capital someday.
What makes someone a good ruler, anyway?
Diogenes says a person needs very little. I think he's mostly right.
Hancock still owes me a copper. I'm sure of it.
Olaf's jokes are terrible. I laugh anyway.
talk_ready: I have something on my mind...
Father, do you have a moment?
There's something I want to ask Father.
I should talk to Father tonight.
Maybe Father will know what to say...
I need to tell Father something.
Father always listens. I should go find him.
I can't stop thinking about something. I should talk to Father.
I wonder if Father has time to talk...
I've been meaning to say something to Father...
